title: 6.17.2 Sub-build: Launch and arc
description: One arm, one stone, one arc. Launch on release and watch gravity bend the shot.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The arm aims. Clicking does nothing: no stone is made.

steps.title: Launch on release
steps.instructions: Inside `if (mouse.released())`, make a stone at the arm, set `direction = arm.rotation` and `speed = 9`, and push it into `shots`.
hints: `direction` and `speed` are the two numbers the arm already knows.
Gravity is on, so the stone arcs by itself.

steps.title: Only one per click
steps.instructions: Run it and click once: one stone. If you get a stream, the make is outside the release test.
hints: `mouse.presses()` fires on the way down; `released()` on the way up. Either is one frame.

requirements.title: Made on release, kept
requirements.description: A new Sprite is made inside mouse.released() and pushed into an array. Help: 6.17.1 (Reading: Launching on release)

requirements.title: Sent along the arm
requirements.description: The shot gets direction (and speed), not a random push. Help: 6.17.1 (Reading: Launching on release)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Launch and arc". The task: make a shot on mouse.released(), at the arm, with direction from the arm rotation and a speed, and keep it in an array. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: One per release
rubric.description: The shot is made inside the release test.

rubric.title: Direction from the arm
rubric.description: The shot leaves along the arm, not at a fixed angle.
